title: Eviction-windowed prefetch lanes and kernel tiering for fragmented KV pages
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement: In production paged-attention workloads we see frequent mid-sequence stalls caused by two correlated phenomena: (1) fragmentation of the KV cache across pages leading to many small scattered reads during prefill/decoding, and (2) suboptimal kernel selection when the runtime assumes contiguous hot segments. This increases p95/p99 decode latency and raises token cost due to repeated small kernel invocations and re-decode fallback.

Goal: Implement an eviction-windowed prefetch lane combined with a fragment-aware kernel tiering policy that jointly reduces decode stalls and improves kernel efficiency for fragmented KV pages. The solution should be transparent to callers, configurable per-tenant, and measurable via existing perf dashboards.

High-level approach:
- Eviction-windowed prefetch lanes: create a lightweight prefetch queue that attaches to eviction windows (recently-evicted or about-to-be-evicted page ranges). When a request's decode horizon overlaps such a window, enqueue a targeted prefetch that pulls minimal fragments required to satisfy the next N decode steps. Prefetch lanes have adjustable aggressiveness (bytes/sec budget and TTL).
- Fragment-aware kernel tiering: extend the kernel selector to consult a fragmentation score for the requested page set. Low-fragment (contiguous hot pages) requests use the highest-throughput fused kernels; high-fragment requests route to a conservative tier that uses fragment-consolidating kernels (stitching microreads, coalesced DMA) and a prefill-first decode mode that avoids many tiny kernel launches.
- Coordinated backpressure and quotas: prefetch lanes honor tenant quotas and apply admission control to avoid noisy neighbors. Prefetch operations are priced into the cost accounting so tenants can opt-in.

Acceptance criteria:
- p95 decode latency reduction >= 12% and p99 reduction >= 8% on internal paged-attention benchmark (read-heavy conversational workload) vs baseline.
- Overall token cost change <= +2% (target is neutral or net-negative).
- No increase in out-of-memory incidents in the test fleet.
- Feature flagged rollout and per-tenant tuning available in runtime-2.4 canary.

Out-of-scope: large-scale disk-tiered swap strategies (separate ticket), persistent KV layout changes (defragmentation background job is considered but not implemented here).
comments: 2026-02-19: Initial design writeup uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Eviction-Windowed-Prefetch-Design (internal) -- requested feedback from serving-runtime and infra teams.

2026-02-24: Design review notes: SRE raised concerns about prefetch noise on bursty tenants; agreed to admission control with tenant-level budget. Action: add per-tenant token to config + metrics for prefetch bytes and hit rate. (reviewers: Priya R., Jamal V., Lena H.)

2026-03-02: Spike results: microbench on a 8-GPU dev cluster shows fragment-aware kernel tiering reduces small-read kernel invocations by ~38% and improves end-to-end decode throughput by ~9% for synthetic fragmentation patterns (see PR #1324 experimental branch). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1324

2026-03-05: Implementation PR opened (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1388 -- includes prefetch lane queue, fragmentation scorer, and kernel selector hooks. Unit tests + fuzzer added for shard accounting.

2026-03-07: Perf dashboard snapshot: internal/dashboard?run=eviction-prefetch-20260307 shows p95 improvement 14% on read-heavy conv workload, p99 improvement 9%. Early signal looks good but need longer soak to validate memory behavior.

2026-03-09: QA found a regression in tenant A where aggressive prefetch caused increased decoder memory peaks during bursty traffic (repro in canary). Temporary mitigation: lower default prefetch budget and enable conservative kernel tier by default for canary tenants. Root cause under investigation: prefetch TTL not respecting eviction budget when multiple requests interleave.

2026-03-10: Action items added: (1) implement prefetch coalescing across concurrent requests to reduce duplicate reads, (2) add eviction-window aging heuristics to prevent repeated re-prefetch of same fragments. Assigned to: Alejandro Ruiz.

Links to artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Eviction-Windowed-Prefetch-Design, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1388, perf runs: https://perf.redwood.ai/runs/eviction-prefetch-20260307
implementation_notes: Fragmentation scorer: lightweight approximate metric using page occupancy bitmap + LRU distance sampling. Score in [0,100] where >45 considered fragmented.
Kernel tiering policy: selector consults (fragmentation_score, estimated_io_ops, seq_len) -> {fused_fast, stitched_conservative}. Add hysteresis to avoid thrash on score jitter.
Prefetch lane design: FIFO per-eviction-window with coalescing by (tenant, page_range). Budget enforced with a token-bucket (configurable: default 4MB/s per-tenant).

Backpressure: prefetches are deprioritized when decode queue depth > 8 or GPU util > 85%. Prefetch futures advertise expected completion time to decoder so decode scheduler can choose immediate kernel vs wait-for-prefetch.
Testing: unit tests for scorer determinism, integration test injecting synthetic fragmentation, long soak in canary for 7 days with metrics collection (memory, OOM, p95/p99).
